name: Downer EDI Limited
listing_note: DOW.NZ is a secondary, foreign-exempt NZX listing of an ASX-primary stock (ASX: DOW, ~A$6.60-6.66, market cap ~A$4.2-4.3bn as of Sept-2026, down ~9% over the prior year despite the FY26 earnings beat). The NZX line is illiquid to the point of showing near-zero trades; third-party data feeds have historically served stale quotes on the NZX ticker. This is a data artefact, not a real price. Any NZ investor buying 'DOW.NZ' is economically buying the ASX-listed, AUD-denominated stock, and valuation, liquidity and currency exposure should all be assessed off the ASX line, not the NZX quote.
overview: Downer EDI is Australasia's largest integrated services and infrastructure contractor, maintaining and building essential infrastructure -- roads, rail rolling stock and transit systems, power, gas, water, telecommunications networks, and government/defence facilities -- across Australia and New Zealand. It operates through three reporting segments (Transport, Energy & Utilities, Facilities) on a portfolio of long-term, largely government and quasi-government contracts. The company reports in AUD with a 30 June fiscal year end, and its primary listing is ASX: DOW; DOW.NZ is a thinly-traded secondary line.

business_model.summary: Downer earns fee/margin income from multi-year operations-and-maintenance and project-delivery contracts with government agencies, utilities and large corporates. Revenue is very large (~A$9.8bn FY2026 pro forma, down 4.6% YoY as portfolio simplification continues) relative to profit -- this is a low-single-digit-margin contracting model where small percentage swings in EBITA margin move earnings materially. Work-in-hand reached $38.5bn at 30-Jun-2026 (+10% YoY, on $12.2bn of new work secured in the year and extending into FY32 and beyond), of which approximately 93% is services-based (recurring maintenance) and approximately 90% is government-related, giving the revenue base a largely recurring, contracted character rather than pure project/transactional risk.

revenue_streams.name: Transport (roads, rail & transit systems, NZ projects, rail rolling-stock manufacturing)
revenue_streams.trend: declining revenue (-3.3% FY26) but margin-accretive (+6.8% EBITA, 5.7% margin); large NZ projects rolling off, offset by new NZ state highway/water contract wins

revenue_streams.name: Energy & Utilities (power projects/transmission, gas, water, telecommunications)
revenue_streams.trend: revenue declining (-10.9% FY26, portfolio simplification/NBN completion) but margin expanding strongly (+20% EBITA, 5.7% margin) on power transition and water-sector wins (~A$1.5bn)

revenue_streams.name: Facilities (Government/Integrated Facilities Management, Defence Estate Maintenance)
revenue_streams.trend: revenue slightly down (-1.8% FY26), highest-margin segment (6.8%) but EBITA declined -4.8% on the EMOS-to-PAS Defence contract transition

business_model.customer_type: Overwhelmingly B2G/quasi-government (federal, state, defence agencies) and large regulated utilities/corporates (e.g. Chevron, Transurban, Stockland); approximately 90% of work-in-hand is government-related
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly Australia with a material New Zealand transport/roads business; NZD-denominated revenue is a meaningful minority and has created FX translation headwinds in AUD reporting during periods of NZD weakness

main_competitors: Keolis (rail/transit, formerly a Downer JV partner, now fully independent since Dec-2025)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the two or three largest diversified infrastructure-services contractors in Australia/NZ (alongside Ventia and UGL); leading position in road maintenance and rail services in Australasia and a top-tier defence facilities contractor

moat_factors.description: Long-dated maintenance contracts (often 5-10 years, work-in-hand now extending into FY32+) on essential infrastructure create high switching costs for government customers, embedded local knowledge, plant and workforce; re-tendering cycles are, however, a recurring source of both risk and opportunity

Large performance bonding facilities and a Fitch BBB issuer rating give Downer capacity to bid and be awarded large multi-year government contracts (e.g. the $3.05bn Defence PAS contract) that smaller players cannot bond
Exposure spread across roads, rail, power, water, telco and defence facilities reduces single-sector cyclicality versus pure-play peers

Reputation was materially damaged by the FY2023 accounting scandal and subsequent regulatory/legal actions (shareholder class action, ACCC cartel case); being rebuilt under new management with three consecutive years of margin improvement, but both legal matters remain unresolved and continue to weigh on sentiment and financing costs

weaknesses: Structurally thin margins (underlying EBITA margin 5.1% in FY26, still below the FY30 target of 'approaching 6%') leave limited buffer against cost overruns or contract mispricing

Heavy reliance on government tendering cycles and public infrastructure/agency budgets that can be cut or delayed by political change (softer Australian state Transport agency spend cited repeatedly across FY25/FY26)

History of poor contract risk management (the FY2023 Utilities WIP/revenue-recognition scandal, and multiple 'underperforming contracts' exited through FY25/FY26) suggests execution and internal-control risk is not yet fully proven over a full cycle
Labour- and subcontractor-intensive cost base exposes margins to wage inflation and subcontractor availability

FY26 revenue declined 4.6% (pro forma) even as margins improved, and management has flagged 1H FY27 revenue and earnings expected lower than the prior-year period before a second-half recovery -- growth has not yet resumed

growth_drivers: Energy transition-related capex: transmission line and substation construction within Power Projects is a clear structural growth pocket (Energy & Utilities EBITA +20% in FY26), offsetting the winding-down of NBN telco build-out work

Defence spending growth: the Defence Property and Asset Services (PAS) contract ($3.05bn, 6-year term, commenced Feb-2026) replaces the prior EMOS arrangement and, once past the FY26 margin-reset transition period, is expected to normalise to a higher-margin steady state

Portfolio simplification/margin mix shift: completed divestment of low-margin Cleaning, Catering and Laundries businesses and the full exit from the Keolis Downer JV (completed Dec-2025) has structurally lifted group EBITA margin to 5.1% in FY26 (from 4.4% in FY25 and 2.9% in 1H25) by removing dilutive, higher-risk revenue

Work-in-hand growth: total work-in-hand rose 10% to $38.5bn at 30-Jun-2026 on $12.2bn of new work secured in the year, including the Defence PAS contract, ~A$1.5bn of water-sector wins, and NZ$1.5bn of New Zealand Transport Agency contracts -- a strong forward indicator with visibility now extending into FY32 and beyond

New Zealand State Highway contracts: NZ$1.5bn of New Zealand Transport Agency (Waka Kotahi) contracts secured, including the NZD$311m Project Alliance Agreement (2NL South Alliance, Otaki-to-North-of-Levin highway) -- a confirmed tailwind for the previously soft NZ Transport business

Capital return: on-market buyback (up to A$260m, ~5% of issued capital) with A$96.5m (~37% of the program) executed in FY26, continuing into FY27; combined with a 65% payout ratio and dividends raised 17% to 29.2 cents per share fully franked, signalling management/board confidence in free cash generation

Diversification beyond pure-government Facilities customers: A$500m, five-year Integrated Facilities Management contract with Stockland (commencing 1-Aug-2026) and A$310m Transurban Sydney motorway maintenance contract broaden the private-sector customer base

Formal medium-term targets set at the FY26 result: 4-5% revenue CAGR through FY30, EBITA margin approaching 6% by FY30, and underlying EPS CAGR of 9% from FY25 to FY28 -- giving investors an explicit multi-year roadmap for the first time since the FY2023 reset

business.description: Large single contracts (e.g. a Victorian power maintenance contract not renewed in 2025, the EMOS-to-PAS Defence transition causing a margin reset through FY26) show that loss or unfavourable renegotiation of any major contract can swing group earnings meaningfully given thin overall margins

At a ~5.1% underlying EBITA margin (still below the FY30 'approaching 6%' target), cost overruns, weather disruption or a handful of mispriced contracts can erase a large share of group profit, as demonstrated by the FY2023 scandal and repeated 'underperforming contract' exits through FY25/FY26

FY26 pro forma revenue fell 4.6% and management has explicitly guided 1H FY27 revenue and earnings lower than the prior-year period before an expected second-half recovery; the FY30 4-5% revenue CAGR target has not yet begun to show up in reported numbers

business.risk: New Zealand and Australian Transport softness
business.description: Australian Road Services volumes remain impacted by reduced state Transport agency spend, and large legacy NZ projects are rolling off, though this is partially offset by new NZ state highway maintenance, water and alliance wins

financial.description: Fitch has maintained a BBB issuer rating; the rating explicitly depends on maintaining underlying EBITDA margin above a covenant-style threshold, and Downer continues to manage AUD MTN refinancing through bridge facilities and bank lines
NZD-denominated revenue translated into AUD reporting currency creates translation headwinds/tailwinds depending on NZD/AUD movements

financial.risk: Leverage headroom is comfortable but capital is being returned aggressively
financial.description: Net debt/EBITDA improved further to 0.8x at 30-Jun-2026 (from 0.9x, well inside the <1.5x internal target), but A$286m of FY26 shareholder returns (A$189m dividends + A$96.5m buyback), with the buyback continuing into FY27, reduces the cushion available if earnings disappoint

regulatory.description: A consolidated Victorian Supreme Court class action (Maurice Blackburn lead) alleges Downer misled the market over FY20-23 Utilities revenue/WIP misreporting, covering shareholders who acquired stock between 23-Jul-2019 and 24-Feb-2023. A court-ordered mediation was scheduled to commence by 12-Dec-2025. As of this analysis (Sept-2026), no public confirmation of a settlement or mediation outcome has been located -- the matter remains a live, unresolved contingent liability disclosed in the FY2026 accounts, and if unsettled would be expected to proceed toward trial. Downer has cross-claimed against former auditor KPMG, which resigned as auditor as a result and was separately joined as a direct defendant by plaintiffs, with KPMG filing a third-party claim back against Downer.

The ACCC's Federal Court civil cartel proceedings against Downer subsidiary Spotless Facility Services and Ventia Australia (with related BGIS allegations) and four senior executives, alleging Defence estate-maintenance price-fixing between April 2019 and August 2022, remain ongoing. As of early Sept-2026 the case is in pre-trial document/conferral stages -- a judge publicly criticised the parties for failing to finalise trial-preparation documents -- indicating trial has not yet occurred. Downer continues to deny the allegations. Penalties, costs and executive disqualification orders remain sought by the regulator with no ruling or settlement publicly confirmed.

Heightened regulator and customer scrutiny following the accounting scandal and ACCC action increases the risk of exclusion from, or added compliance cost in, future government tenders -- though Downer continued to win large new Defence, water and government contracts through the case's pendency, suggesting limited practical tendering impact so far

macro.description: Revenue is ~90% government-related; state and federal budget tightening, election cycles or shifts in infrastructure priorities directly affect contract volumes, as already seen in soft AU Transport agency spend and the FY26 revenue decline
Employee benefits and subcontractor costs are the two largest cost lines; wage inflation or skilled-labour shortages in Australia/NZ construction and utilities markets pressure margins directly
Management guidance has repeatedly been conditioned on 'no material weather disruptions,' underscoring seasonal/climate risk to outdoor infrastructure work
Net finance costs remain a meaningful P&L line; rate moves affect refinancing cost and the group's net debt plus lease liabilities, though leverage at 0.8x net debt/EBITDA limits the direct impact

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Positive structural demand from the energy transition (transmission/substation build-out), rising Australian defence spending, water-sector investment, and population-growth-driven infrastructure investment; offset by a mature/completing NBN telecommunications cycle and cautious state government transport-agency budgets that have driven near-term revenue declines
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. Recurring maintenance work (~93% of work-in-hand) smooths some cyclicality, but project-delivery revenue (major rail/transit builds, road construction) is more cyclical and tied to public capex cycles and election-driven budget decisions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via financing costs and via government capex appetite; direct balance-sheet sensitivity is currently modest given improved leverage (0.8x net debt/EBITDA)
key_input_costs: Steel/raw materials and consumables for rail and infrastructure builds

recent_developments.event: On-market buyback (up to A$230-260m, ~5% of issued capital) formally commenced, running into FY2027
Registration deadline (10-Sep-2025) closed for group members in the consolidated shareholder class action over the FY20-23 accounting irregularities
Completed sale of remaining 49% interest in Keolis Downer transit JV to Keolis Group (completed 1-Dec-2025), finalising Downer's full exit from that rail/transit JV

Court-ordered mediation in the shareholder class action was scheduled to commence by 12-Dec-2025; no public confirmation of a settlement or outcome has been located as of Sept-2026 -- treated as unresolved and still pending

H1-2026 (half year to 31-Dec-2025) result: statutory NPAT $98.0m (+30%), underlying NPATA $136.1m (+7.0%), underlying EBITA margin improved to 4.6% (from 3.7%), work-in-hand up 8.9% to $38.2bn, net debt/EBITDA improved to 0.8x from 1.3x, interim dividend raised 19% to 12.9cps (100% franked); Fitch reaffirmed BBB issuer rating; FY2026 underlying NPATA guidance of $295-315m issued
Secured a new A$310m contract with Transurban to maintain Sydney's motorway network, and a new A$500m, five-year Integrated Facilities Management contract with Stockland commencing 1-Aug-2026
Secured ~A$1.5bn of water-sector contract wins and NZ$1.5bn of New Zealand Transport Agency (Waka Kotahi) contracts, including the confirmed NZD$311m 2NL South Alliance project alliance agreement

FY2026 full-year result (year to 30-Jun-2026) reported: pro forma revenue $9.8bn (-4.6%), underlying EBITA $502.9m (+6%), underlying EBITA margin 5.1% (up from 4.4% in FY25, ahead of the >4.5% target), statutory NPAT $225.4m (+51-58%), underlying NPATA $306.7m (+10%, within the $295-315m guidance range), final dividend 16.3cps (100% franked, full-year dividends 29.2cps, +17%), work-in-hand up 10% to $38.5bn on $12.2bn of new work, net debt/EBITDA 0.8x (from 0.9x), cash conversion 91% (vs >90% target), underlying EPS 42.9cps (3-year CAGR 26%)

Management issued FY2030 medium-term targets: 4-5% revenue CAGR through FY30, underlying EBITA margin approaching 6% by FY30, cash conversion >90% average, and underlying EPS CAGR of 9% from FY25 to FY28; guided that 1H FY27 revenue and earnings are expected below the prior-year period, with growth resuming in 2H FY27

Shares fell on the results release despite the earnings beat, as investors focused on the softer FY27 revenue outlook and the EMOS-to-PAS Defence transition margin drag; consensus analyst price targets (~A$7.8-7.9) remained well above the trading price (~A$6.6), a gap that widened after the result

ACCC price-fixing case against Spotless/Ventia remains in pre-trial phase; a Federal Court judge publicly criticised both parties for delays in finalising trial-preparation documents, indicating the matter has not yet reached trial
Share buyback program approximately 37% complete (A$96.5m of up to A$260m executed in FY26) and continuing into FY27

items.target: 1H FY27 revenue below 1H FY26; full FY27 revenue and earnings growth expected with 2H recovery; medium-term 4-5% revenue CAGR FY26-FY30
items.vs_prior: new (first explicit multi-year revenue target since the FY2023 reset)
items.notes: FY26 pro forma revenue fell 4.6% to $9.8bn as portfolio simplification continued; management now guiding a near-term dip before renewed growth

items.vs_prior: raised / extended (continuation of the multi-year margin-recovery trend, now with an explicit FY30 endpoint)
items.notes: FY26 margin of 5.1% beat the prior >4.5% target; EMOS-to-PAS Defence contract transition is expected to be a near-term drag before normalising
FY26 underlying EPS of 42.9cps already reflects a 3-year CAGR of 26%, well ahead of this forward target, aided by the ongoing buyback
FY26 cash conversion of 91% exceeded this target
Improved to 0.8x at 30-Jun-2026 from 0.9x a year earlier; comfortably inside target, supporting continued buyback and dividend growth

guidance.management_commentary: Management characterised FY2026 as a year of continued margin recovery -- underlying EBITA margin of 5.1% beat the prior >4.5% target and underlying NPATA of $306.7m landed within the $295-315m guidance range -- driven by portfolio simplification (exit of low-margin Cleaning, Catering, Laundries and the Keolis Downer JV), tighter tendering discipline, and completion/renegotiation of underperforming contracts. For the first time since the FY2023 reset, management set explicit medium-term targets (4-5% revenue CAGR and ~6% EBITA margin by FY30, 9% EPS CAGR to FY28), signalling confidence the turnaround is durable. However, management also flagged that 1H FY27 revenue and earnings are expected to be lower than the prior-year period, with growth resuming in the second half, reflecting the ongoing EMOS-to-PAS Defence contract margin transition and the tail of portfolio-simplification revenue attrition. Shares fell on the results release despite the earnings beat, as the market focused on the softer near-term outlook rather than the medium-term targets.

bull_case: A genuine, multi-year margin turnaround is now proven across three full years: underlying EBITA margin rose from 2.9% (1H25) to 5.1% (FY26), beating the prior >4.5% target, with management now committing to explicit FY30 targets (~6% margin, 4-5% revenue CAGR, 9% EPS CAGR to FY28) for the first time since the FY2023 reset

Balance sheet has been meaningfully repaired and capital returns are accelerating -- net debt/EBITDA down to 0.8x, a Fitch BBB rating maintained, A$286m returned to shareholders in FY26 (A$189m dividends + A$96.5m buyback, ~37% of the up-to-A$260m program complete and continuing into FY27), with dividends up 17% to 29.2cps fully franked

~90% government-related, ~93% services work-in-hand ($38.5bn, +10% in FY26 on $12.2bn of new work, extending into FY32+) provides unusual revenue visibility for a contracting business, underpinned by structural tailwinds in defence spend (PAS contract), the energy transition, water-sector investment, and confirmed new NZ Transport contracts (NZ$1.5bn)

Divestment program (Laundries, Catering, Cleaning, Keolis Downer JV) has removed the lowest-margin, highest-risk parts of the portfolio, and new private-sector wins (Stockland A$500m IFM, Transurban A$310m) show the recovering business can win work beyond government customers

Valuation gap is wide and the market may be under-pricing the turnaround: the stock trades around A$6.6 versus consensus price targets of ~A$7.8-7.9 (a ~20% gap that widened after the FY26 result), and neither major legal overhang (class action, ACCC case) has yet crystallised a negative financial outcome despite being live for over a year
bear_case: Two significant unresolved legal/regulatory overhangs persist well over a year after they emerged -- the consolidated shareholder class action over FY20-23 accounting irregularities (mediation occurred by Dec-2025 with no settlement publicly confirmed as of Sept-2026) and the ACCC Federal Court price-fixing proceedings against Spotless (alongside Ventia, with related BGIS allegations), which remains in pre-trial conferral with a judge openly criticising delays -- creating open-ended binary tail risk to both cash and reputation with no visible resolution date

Growth has stalled even as margins improved: FY26 pro forma revenue fell 4.6% to $9.8bn, and management has explicitly guided 1H FY27 revenue and earnings below the prior-year period, meaning the FY30 4-5% revenue CAGR target has not yet begun to show up and near-term newsflow could disappoint

Margins remain structurally thin (~5.1% EBITA, still below the FY30 ~6% target) in a labour- and subcontractor-heavy business, meaning the current 'turnaround' could as easily reverse on a handful of mispriced contracts as it improved from disciplined exits -- the FY2023 scandal itself began as contract-level misreporting

Government-contract concentration cuts both ways: the EMOS-to-PAS Defence transition margin reset already dragged FY26 Facilities EBITA down 4.8% despite the segment's highest margin, and ~90% government exposure leaves the business fully at the mercy of public infrastructure budget cycles and re-tender outcomes

The stock fell on the FY26 results release despite an earnings beat, as investors focused on the softer FY27 outlook -- a pattern suggesting the market is discounting the medium-term FY30 targets until nearer-term growth actually resumes, and the shares have underperformed with market cap down ~9% over the trailing year

The DOW.NZ line itself is effectively untradeable/illiquid, meaning any NZ-domiciled holder is really underwriting ASX-line, AUD-denominated risk and currency exposure while getting none of the liquidity benefit of a real local market -- a structural, non-fundamental risk specific to accessing this name via the NZX ticker
